# Practitioner Academy Proposal

**Client:** Tamarack Instruments
**Prepared for:** Dana Whitfield, General Counsel
**Program:** Practitioner Academy, AI Governance Academy
**Format:** 2 days, live virtual, four 90-minute working sessions per day
**Price:** US$12,500

## 1. Situation Summary

Dana Whitfield, this proposal draws only on the Client Profile Block. Tamarack Instruments designs and manufactures laboratory measurement instruments. It is headquartered in the Netherlands and operates in the Netherlands, Germany and the United States.

The Profile Block records the following:

* **AI use cases:**
  * A customer service chatbot on the support portal (deployed).
  * AI visual inspection on the German production line (piloting).
  * AI sales forecasting (planned for next year).
* **AI maturity:** Piloting.
* **Regulatory drivers:** the EU AI Act and GDPR.
* **Certification target:** ISO/IEC 42001, with work to start next year. The start date is noted as not fixed.
* **Risk event:** an internal audit finding of June 2026 recording no inventory of AI systems.
* **Incumbent frameworks:** ISO/IEC 27001 ISMS, ISO 9001 quality management system and internal audit function.

Your stated objective is: "I want governance in place before visual inspection goes into production in Q2 2027."

## 2. Why Practitioner Capability Fits Now

The Practitioner Academy is a working program. Participants leave with governance artifacts started in the repositories they will keep using, not only with notes. Four Profile Block facts make it a fit at this point:

* **A dated target.** Your stated objective sets Q2 2027 as the point by which governance should be in place for visual inspection.
* **A named gap.** The June 2026 finding names the absence of an AI inventory, which is the first artifact the program starts.
* **Three use cases at three stages.** Deployed, piloting and planned systems give participants a full lifecycle to practise on.
* **Mixed audience roles.** General Counsel, CISO, Head of Quality, Head of Data, German plant manager and two internal auditors can build shared artifacts in the same sessions.

The program teaches three principles, carried through every exercise:

* **Slow AI**
* **Informed Intent**
* **Final Liability rests with the Human**

The program does not promise any certification or audit outcome. Classification and risk judgements drafted in session remain drafts for review by the Client.

## 3. Running Worked Examples

Two use cases run across both days:

* **AI visual inspection** is the primary example because it is the subject of your stated objective.
* **The customer service chatbot** is the second example because it is the deployed system and because the Profile Block states that customer data must stay in the EU.

**AI sales forecasting** enters the inventory and the intake procedure as the planned case. This tests how a new system would be brought under governance before it is built.

**Constraint handling.** Every exercise uses sanitized analogs:

* **Chatbot exercises** use synthetic support tickets, clearly labelled as synthetic.
* **Visual inspection exercises** use synthetic defect descriptions for a generic instrument component.

No customer data and no data about production staff enters the sessions or the repositories. Nothing produced in the program is applied to production staff. This respects the stated requirement that the German works council is consulted before anything touches production staff.

## 4. Curriculum Spine and Exercises

Participants work directly in two repositories:

* **GRC Workbook:** https://github.com/rolldabones/grc-workbook
* **Slow AI Kitchen:** https://github.com/rolldabones/slow-ai-kitchen

Two reference repositories support specific sessions:

* **AI Governance for Boards** (https://github.com/rolldabones/ai-governance-for-boards) is the board-layer reference in Session 1.
* **The Definition of Done** (https://github.com/rolldabones/definition-of-done) is the acceptance-layer reference in Session 8.

**Day 1: GRC Workbook**

| Session | Exercise and worked example | Repository asset | Artifact |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1. Governance structures | Tell *The Turtle and the Phoenix*, then use the handle map to bridge into the workbook. Draft decision rights for all three use cases, with each accountable human left as a named placeholder to confirm. Close with the kit's twenty-minute closing exercise. | Facilitation kit (https://github.com/rolldabones/AI-Governance-Academy/blob/main/the-turtle-and-the-phoenix.md): story text, handle map and section 8. GRC Workbook module: governance structures. Board-layer reference for escalation design. | Draft decision rights matrix, plus the three artifacts of the kit's section 8 |
| 2. AI system inventories and classification | Enter the chatbot, visual inspection and sales forecasting into the inventory. Draft EU AI Act and GDPR classification fields, marked for legal review. | GRC Workbook module: AI system inventories and classification | Started AI inventory with three entries |
| 3. Risk and impact assessments | Draft risk entries for visual inspection and the chatbot, including an EU data residency entry for the chatbot analog. | GRC Workbook module: risk and impact assessments | Draft risk register entries |
| 4. Policies and operating procedures | Draft an AI use policy outline and a new-system intake procedure, then test the procedure against sales forecasting. | GRC Workbook module: policies and operating procedures | Draft policy outline and intake procedure |

The fable is run on Day 1 so that the doctrine is seated before the Slow AI Kitchen instruments arrive on Day 2.

**Day 2: Slow AI Kitchen plus assurance**

| Session | Exercise and worked example | Repository asset | Artifact |
|---|---|---|---|
| 5. Governed prompting | Build a governed prompt set for the chatbot analog, with the intent of each prompt recorded. | Slow AI Kitchen pattern: governed prompting | Governed prompt set with intent records |
| 6. Practical AI workflow design | Design governed workflows for the visual inspection analog and the chatbot analog. | Slow AI Kitchen pattern: practical AI workflow design | Two governed workflows |
| 7. Human oversight and accountability | Place human review points and escalation routes in both workflows. Include works council consultation as a gate before any production staff impact. | Slow AI Kitchen pattern: human oversight and accountability | Oversight and escalation map |
| 8. Evidence collection and audit readiness | Define the evidence each artifact must produce, and acceptance criteria for calling it done. | GRC Workbook module: evidence collection and audit readiness. Definition of Done as the acceptance-layer reference. | Evidence plan and acceptance criteria |

## 5. Deliverables

* Started AI system inventory (three entries)
* Draft risk register entries
* At least two governed workflows (visual inspection and chatbot analogs)
* Draft decision rights matrix, policy outline and intake procedure
* Governed prompt set, oversight and escalation map and evidence plan
* The three artifacts of section 8 of the facilitation kit

All artifacts are drafts held in the Client's working copies of the repositories. Finishing them remains with the Client.

## 6. Logistics and Price

* **Format:** 2 days, live virtual, four 90-minute working sessions per day.
* **Price:** US$12,500. This sits within the stated budget ceiling of US$80,000 this fiscal year.
* **Dates:** Unknown.
* **Participant list:** Unknown, to be confirmed against the audience roles in the Profile Block.

## 7. Questions to Confirm at Intake

1. Where should the Client's working copies of the repositories be hosted, so that the EU data constraint is respected?
2. Does any program activity require works council consultation in advance?
3. Does the chatbot process customer data, and where?
4. Which existing records under the ISO/IEC 27001 ISMS or the ISO 9001 quality management system, if any, may be referenced in exercises?
5. Which body receives AI governance reporting?
6. Who will attend, and on what dates?

## 8. Next Step

A decision is expected by 15 December 2026. On confirmation, we will schedule the intake call to resolve the questions above and fix program dates.

Human-made, for Easy Work, Simply Done.
